question: Can exact monotone linear luminance plus analytically bounded zero-luminance chroma retain the characteristic look without boundary or luminance-order failures?

operator.luminance: Y is mapped by the exact epsilon-anchored CB10 scalar characteristic curve, making output luminance globally monotone and independent of chroma
operator.chroma: C=RGB-Y has exact weighted sum zero; output=Y_mapped+k*C with one analytically maximal k in [0,1] satisfying cube bounds and stricter epsilon bounds only for source-interior channels
operator.forbidden: hard clipping, post-hoc Lab gamut compression, spatial smoothing, curve refit or strength rescue

stop_rules: Do not change luminance weights, curve, strength, epsilon, chroma-scale equation, population, controls or gates after candidate pixels are scored.
Any automatic failure closes this exact luma/chroma executor before visual review and without rescue.
Pass opens severe visual review only and cannot establish Velvia calibration, authenticity, preference or product promotion.
claim_ceiling: Rights-cleared photographic development evidence for exact-luminance analytically bounded chroma execution of a retained reversal characteristic shape; not Velvia calibration, authenticity, preference or product promotion.
